summary: Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Eishun Fushimi studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.
A Buddhist studies scholar, Eiyin Yasuda studied under Gyōin Hashimoto around 1950 and completed studies at Ryukoku University between circa 1957 and 1961.
Eizan Tatsuta was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Sokatsu Shaku and founded Ningen Zen Kyodan.

Ekai Kawaguchi worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying at Doshisha University, Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College. He served as rector at Gohyaku Rakan-ji (c. 1887–1891) and professor at Toyo University (1916).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Eki Nakayama studied at Kyoto University and held a DC2 special researcher fellowship with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (both attested 2020).
A Buddhist studies scholar, Ekkyo Uno held posts as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a commissioned researcher at Honganji Sōgakuin (attested 1998).

Eleanor Nesbitt, a scholar of religious studies and Indology, studied at Girton College, Cambridge, and the University of Oxford. She served as professor at the University of Warwick from circa 1989 and founded the Punjab Research Group.

Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, Eleanor Rosch earned her bachelor's at Reed College and PhD at Harvard University under Roger Brown. She held positions at Brown University, Connecticut College, and the University of California, Berkeley (from 1971).

A Tibetology scholar, Elena De Rossi Filibeck studied East Asian history under Luciano Petech at the University of Rome (c. 1967–1971). She held posts at the University of Bonn (c. 1976–1977) and the University of Rome (1980).
Elena France Hanson specializes in Buddhist and religious studies, completing her Doctor of Philosophy at Harvard University under the supervision of Charles Hallisey.

An Indologist and religious studies scholar, Elena Mucciarelli studied at the University of Tübingen, where she also held a post (2016–2017). In 2020, she became an assistant professor and Gonda Lecturer at the University of Groningen.

Eli Franco works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, having studied at Tel Aviv University, EPHE, Paris Nanterre, and Hamburg. He held positions at La Trobe, Vienna, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and Leipzig (2004–2021).
Elijah Sacvan Ary, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University under Janet Gyatso and Leonard van der Kuijp.

Specializing in philosophy and Indology, Eliot Deutsch earned his PhD at Columbia University. He taught at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi from 1967 to 2006.

An Indologist and philosopher, Elisa Freschi earned her doctorate under Raffaele Torella. She held academic posts at the University of Rome, the University of Vienna, and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

A religious studies scholar, Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza studied at Würzburg and Münster. She held professorships at the University of Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard University from 1988.

Elizabeth A. Cecil works in Indology, religious studies, and archaeology, earning degrees from Hastings College, University of Tennessee, and Brown University. She held positions at Leiden University, University of Groningen, and Florida State University (attested 2021).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and sinology, Elizabeth Anne Morrison studied under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. She held teaching positions at Amherst College (1998–1999) and Middlebury College (attested 2008).

Working in religious studies and Indology, Elizabeth De Michelis studied at SOAS and the University of Cambridge, where she served as director in 2000. She has also been affiliated with the University of Oxford's faculty of theology.

Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned her PhD from the University of Oxford in 1999, studying under doctoral supervisor Alexis Sanderson and teacher Harunaga Isaacson.
